te: Approaches to the debts of Rehabilitation Fund members who are debtors of farmer institutions
se: Agenda: solving the debt problems of farmers who are members of the Farmers Rehabilitation and Development Fund and debtors of farmer institutions, and state policy to help cooperatives and their members, with the Office of the Farmers Rehabilitation and Development Fund, the Bank for Agriculture and Agricultural Cooperatives, the Department of Agricultural Extension, the Cooperative Auditing Department and representatives of agricultural cooperatives invited (the Senate has not yet published the summary of this meeting, so this text is the agenda in the meeting notice, not a resolution of the meeting)
it: Solving the debt problems of farmers who are members of the Farmers Rehabilitation and Development Fund and debtors of farmer institutions, and state policy to help cooperatives and their members

te: Preparing to invite agencies to discuss approaches to cooperative debt rehabilitation
se: The meeting prepared to invite representatives of the Farmers Rehabilitation and Development Fund to discuss support for cooperatives and their members. It noted that site visits had found misunderstandings about debt repayment by cooperative members, which affect the cooperatives. It resolved to invite the Office of the Farmers Rehabilitation and Development Fund, the Bank for Agriculture and Agricultural Cooperatives, the Cooperative Promotion Department, the Cooperative Auditing Department and representatives of agricultural cooperatives to give information at the next meeting
it: Preparing to invite agencies to give information on cooperative support and solving debt problems

te: Summary of the cooperative study visit to Suphan Buri Province
se: Agenda: summary of the study visit on cooperatives in the agricultural sector, Suphan Buri Province, 17 December 2025 (the Senate has not yet published the summary of this meeting, so this text is the agenda in the meeting notice, not a resolution of the meeting)
it: Summary of the study visit on cooperatives in the agricultural sector, Suphan Buri Province, 17 December 2025

te: Urgent and long-term proposals revised before submission to the committee
se: The meeting considered the conclusions and recommendations of the draft report on food security and food safety in the agricultural sector. It revised the urgent proposals, such as self-reliance, access to food and food market development, and the long-term proposal on moving towards sustainable agriculture. It resolved to make the revisions agreed at the meeting and then submit the report to the Committee on Agriculture and Cooperatives
it: Draft report on food security and food safety in the agricultural sector: urgent and long-term recommendations

te: Draft report: proposals to be concise and practical, and to state the Senate's role
se: The meeting considered the overall conclusions and recommendations of the draft report on food security and food safety in the agricultural sector. It felt they should be reviewed to be concise and truly practical, on both food security and food safety, and should state the role of the Senate in recommending ways forward. It resolved to revise the draft report and present the complete version at the next meeting
it: Draft report on food security and food safety in the agricultural sector: conclusions and recommendations

te: Draft report: conclusions on the challenges the agricultural sector faces for food security
se: The meeting considered Chapter 5, conclusions and recommendations, of the draft report on food security and food safety in the agricultural sector. It states that agriculture, as the main source of food production, faces structural challenges such as climate change, the ageing of farmers, production costs, volatile produce prices, the oversight of chemicals and the use of land for industry. The meeting then considered the recommendations further
it: Draft report on food security and food safety in the agricultural sector, Chapter 5: conclusions and recommendations

te: Draft report: the study to be organised by the FAO dimensions of food security
se: The meeting considered the draft report on food security and food safety in the agricultural sector and proposed organising the study by the framework of the Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations (FAO), such as food availability, access to food, food utilisation and food stability
it: Draft study report on food security and food safety in the agricultural sector: dimensions of the study

te: Consideration of the draft study report begins: outline and introduction
se: The meeting considered the draft study report on food security and food safety in the agricultural sector. It considered the report outline and made observations on Chapter 1, the introduction, which sets out the background and objectives of the study: to understand the situation and the factors affecting food safety, and to find ways to strengthen food security
it: Draft study report on food security and food safety in the agricultural sector: outline and introduction

te: Meeting 10/2569 · Subcommittee to Study Food Security
Briefing on the work of provincial food policy councils
se: The meeting heard a representative of the Nonthaburi Provincial Food Policy Council and the director of the Sustainable Agriculture Community Institute on provincial food system strategies, piloted in Nonthaburi and Chiang Mai, to develop a model healthy food system along the whole chain, a food product monitoring system, and policy proposals to promote healthy eating
it: The work of provincial food policy councils

te: Ideas on taxing chemical pesticides heard
se: The meeting heard an academic from the Faculty of Economics, Prince of Songkla University, and a representative of the BioThai Foundation on food safety, in particular the taxing of chemical pesticides, which several countries such as Denmark, Sweden, Norway and France use to reduce the use of farm chemicals, in various forms such as a flat rate or rates by level of hazard
it: Approaches to taxing chemical pesticides, and examples from other countries

te: Briefing by the Hydro-Informatics Institute on water data for agriculture
se: The meeting studied food security and food safety from the angle of water management. It heard the Director of the Hydro-Informatics Institute (Public Organization), who is also a subcommittee member, explain the institute's role as the national hub for water resources data, its use of technology to analyse and forecast the water situation, and the use of the data to support sustainable agricultural production
it: Water management and water data to develop agricultural production inputs

te: Briefing by the natural farming network on promoting organic agriculture
se: The meeting studied the development of farming systems, food safety and food security. It heard representatives of the natural farming network and foundation describe their work promoting organic farming since 1990, which now attracts more interest because of health trends but still faces obstacles, such as switching away from the main cash crops and the lack of systems to collect produce and markets to buy it. The meeting felt that state agencies in each area should help produce concrete results

te: Draft report on sustainably eliminating rabies: recommendations in 6 areas, and further proposals after the Uthai Thani visit
se: The meeting considered the summary, observations and recommendations of the draft study report on an integrated approach to sustainably eliminating rabies, gathering views on recommendations in 6 areas: law; integration; databases; more stray animal shelters that meet standards, including animal quarantine areas; public relations to raise public awareness; and budget support for the agencies concerned to provide staff, tools and modern equipment. It also considered the findings of the study visit on rabies prevention and control and stray dog management in Uthai Thani on 12–13 Nov 2026, with further proposals such as more veterinarians to care for stray animals, budget support for the buildings and systems of the Bangkok stray dog shelter and for sterilisation equipment, a clearer legal definition of stray dogs, and rules for caring for owned dogs or cats that are not being looked after
it: Draft study report on an integrated approach to sustainably eliminating rabies: recommendations in 6 areas (law, integration, databases, stray animal shelters and quarantine areas, public relations and budget)

Findings of the study visit on rabies prevention and control and stray dog management, Uthai Thani, 12–13 Nov 2026: 4 further proposals (veterinary staff, budget for the shelter and sterilisation equipment, the legal definition of stray dogs, and rules for owned animals that are not looked after)

te: Proposal in the draft report: make stray animals a national agenda, with a 15-year strategy
se: The meeting considered the observations and recommendations in the draft report. It felt that solving the problems of stray animals and rabies is still held back by weak links between agencies and incomplete databases. It therefore proposed making the issue a national agenda, preparing a 15-year long-term strategy, setting up a central agency to integrate the work, and developing a central database that links all sectors
it: Observations and recommendations in the draft study report on solving the problem of stray dogs and cats sustainably

te: Meeting summary video · Proposal in the draft report: make stray animals a national agenda, with a 15-year strategy
